title: Momentum and Collisions
seo_title: Momentum Worksheets: p = mv, Collisions and Conservation of Momentum (High School Physics)
standard_text: Use mathematical representations to support the claim that the total momentum of a system of objects is conserved when there is no net force on the system.
meta_desc: Free high school physics worksheets on momentum (NGSS HS-PS2-2): p = mv, conservation of momentum, sticking collisions, recoil and explosions. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: In a closed system, momentum before a collision equals momentum after.
body_html:
How to think about it

Total momentum before = total momentum after (no outside net force).

  • p = mv. Momentum has direction: use + for right and − for left.
  • Sticking collision: m1v1 + m2v2 = (m1 + m2)vf.
  • Starting from rest, the pieces fly apart with equal and opposite momentum.
Example

3 kg at 4 m/s hits 1 kg at rest; they stick. v?

12 ÷ 4

Answer: 3 m/s

Example

50 kg skater pushes 70 kg skater; first moves at 7 m/s. Second?

50 × 7 = 70 × v

Answer: 5 m/s the other way

Common mistakes

  • Thinking momentum is lost in a collision.
  • Ignoring the minus sign for objects moving left.
  • Averaging the speeds instead of using momentum.

faq.a: Momentum is mass times velocity (p = mv). It has direction, like velocity.
When no net outside force acts on the system, the total momentum stays the same in collisions and explosions.

faq.q: How do you solve a sticking collision?
faq.a: Add the momenta before the collision and divide by the total mass to get the shared final velocity.
